rv.q: Much like jazz itself, this production is constantly in conversation with the past, building on existing work without trying to neatly resolve it.
Above all, MILES. draws the audience in with the belief in the genius of the music, and the focus which Benji Akintuyosi, brings to reconciling the character’s contradictions.
It feels only right to tell you, dear readers, to make your way, without delay, to the Little Hall at Southwark Playhouse to see MILES.
MILES. is essential viewing for music lovers, theatregoers, and anyone interested in the cost and the beauty of creation.

This rewarding creative collaboration is, in terms of length, stretched just a little too far and long and loses pace towards the end, but overall offers an intoxicating fusion: audio, visual, performative and experiential.
The music is primary and primal in MILES., offering a snapshot of how feeling, rhythm and skill weave together.

cn.t: Critics praise this immersive Miles Davis two-hander for Benjamin Akintuyosi's powerful performance and its visceral exploration of creative sacrifice, with live trumpet work adding musical authenticity to the intimate production.
